title: High-throughput Identification of Bacteria Repellent Polymers for Medical Devices
protocol: Make up a 2% (w/v) solution of agarose I-B in distilled water.
Heat the suspension in a microwave oven for 30 sec periods until dissolved, ensuring the cap is loosely closed.
Pour the agarose solution into a 100 ml beaker and place it in a 65 °C water bath to maintain a liquid state.
Dip silane-coated slides into the agarose solution, ensuring uniform coating.
Wipe the back of the slide with tissue paper.
Dry the slides, coated side up, in a dust-free environment for at least 24 hours.
Prepare solutions (1% w/v) of selected polymers in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP).
Vortex each polymer solution until fully dissolved.
Fill each well of a 384 microwell plate with 25 µl polymer solution using a micro-pipette.
Ensure no cross contamination occurs, and each well contains a unique polymer.
Use NMP as a negative control in at least two wells.
Record the identity of each polymer solution in each well on a template or spreadsheet file.
Open the software and choose 'Create a new routine'.
Select the 'Description' tab and input experiment details.
Select the 'Head' tab and choose '32-pin microarraying head'.
Select the 'Source' tab, choose plate holder (source plate holder (1x5)), plate type (plate 384 x 6,000), total plates (1) and source order (by columns).
Choose '3x1'' slide' in the 'Slide design' tab.
Input 'Spot view' as layout and set pattern dimensions: Row count (6), Column count (8), Row pitch (750), Column pitch (560).
Select one section to print first.
Input number of slides used for printing in the 'Slide layout' tab.
Select the 'Print' tab, input parameters: Number of stamps per inking (1), number of stamps per spot (5), stamping time (200 msec), inking time (100 msec).
Place agarose-coated slides on the platform.
Ensure a good vacuum seal to hold the slides in position.
Adjust the print-head so that all the pins are at the same height.
Check pin alignment by manually lowering the head onto a glass slide.
Confirm pins move up simultaneously upon manual check.
Adjust any discrepancies in pin height using the sleeve on each pin.
Place the well plate on the plate holder with A1 at top right.
Ensure the well plate is fixed firmly in place.
Use the height adjustor to set an appropriate distance from the bottom of the wells.
Select 'Start' tab and choose 'Run type' as 'Normal'.
Click 'Run' and confirm slide, well plate, etc., are correctly positioned when prompted.
Print 1 section at a time (32 solutions), allowing for cleaning between sections.
Clean pins thoroughly with paper towel dipped in acetone.
Dry the pins using dry tissue paper to ensure they are fully dry.
Place printed microarrays in a slide holder after printing completion.
Dry microarrays overnight in a vacuum oven set at 45 °C.
Sterilize the microarrays with UV light for 30 minutes.
Take a measurement of background fluorescence before inoculating slides with bacteria.
Ensure good aseptic technique during handling of cultures.
Inoculate 5 ml Luria-Bertani broth with a colony from a plate to prepare overnight cultures.
Incubate the cultures overnight at 37 °C, shaking at 200 rpm.
Prepare freezer stocks by adding glycerol (10% concentration) to overnight cultures.
Store the bacterial stock at -80 °C.
Perform serial dilutions of each thawed bacterial stock to determine cell numbers.
Grow bacteria overnight on solid media from the diluted samples.
Prepare single species cultures for application directly to microarrays.
Mix overnights of K. pneumoniae and S. saprophyticus in equal volumes (3 ml each) for BacMix-1.
Dilute the mixed BacMix-1 culture four times with fresh LB to a final volume of 50 ml.
Mix overnights of S. mutans, S. aureus, K. pneumoniae, and E. faecalis in equal volumes (3 ml each) for BacMix-2.
Dilute the mixed BacMix-2 culture four times with fresh LB to a final volume of 50 ml.
Incubate UV-sterilized polymer microarrays with 6 ml of the mixed bacterial cultures at 37 °C with gentle agitation (30 rpm) for 5 days.
Rinse the microarrays twice with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate the microarrays with a solution of 1 µg/ml DAPI stain in PBS for 30 min.
Wash the stained microarray slides in a fresh well plate by swirling gently, changing the PBS once.
Dry the washed microarray slides under a flow of air.
Apply a glass cover slip to the dried microarray slide and seal it with glue.
Sterilize the outer surface of the sealed microarray slide with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Dispose of cultures according to their containment level.
Capture single images for each polymer spot in brightfield and DAPI channels.
Perform image capture manually using a fluorescent microscope with a 20X objective.
Use an automated fluorescence microscope with an X-Y-Z stage controlled by image acquisition software to capture images.
Ensure the gain and exposure time settings are consistent across all microarrays.
Obtain average fluorescence intensity of each spot in the DAPI channel using an image processing software.
Capture images of polymer spots on a replicate microarray incubated only with media without bacteria for background determination.
Deduct background fluorescence from the intensity of each spot to obtain bacterial binding fluorescence.
Calculate average normalized values from four spots representing each polymer.
Identify polymers that exhibit the least bacterial binding as 'hit' polymers.
Prepare solutions of 'hit' polymers at approximately 2% w/v in tetrahydrofuran (THF) or an appropriate solvent.
Spin coat circular glass coverslips with polymer solutions using a spin coater at 2,000 rpm for 10 seconds.
Dry the coated coverslips in a convection oven at 40 °C overnight.
Sterilize the dried coverslips using UV light for 30 minutes prior to inoculating bacteria.
Clean coverslips by plasma treatment for 10 minutes or immersing in 1 M NaOH for 4 hours.
Immerse cleaned coverslips in acetonitrile containing 1% (3-aminopropyl) triethoxysilane overnight.
Clean the coverslips with acetone three times and put into an oven at 100 °C for one hour.
Dip coat the dried coverslips with a 1% agarose aqueous solution maintained in a water bath at 60 °C.
Place the agarose-coated coverslips on a flat surface in dust-free ambient conditions for 24 hours.
Sterilize the agarose-coated coverslips using UV light for 30 minutes prior to inoculating bacteria.
Incubate coverslips with bacteria.
Wash uncoated and coated coverslips twice with 0.1 M cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4).
Fix samples with 2.5% (w/v) glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4) for 2 hr.
Post-fix samples with 1% (w/v) osmium tetroxide for 1 hr at room temperature.
Dehydrate samples sequentially with ethanol washes at 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100% (v/v) for 30 min each.
Dry samples in CO2 according to standard protocols.
Coat samples in a gold/palladium alloy (60/40%) using a sputter coater with current at 30 mA and vacuum at 0.75 Torr.
Examine samples under an electron microscope as per standard protocols.
Visually compare images of the uncoated coverslips and those coated with agarose or 'hit' polymers to confirm bacterial binding/repelling abilities of the polymers.
Choose the most promising 'hit' non-binding polymers for coating medical devices such as central venous catheters.
Evaluate various solvents for their compatibility with the indwelling part of the catheter and their ability to dissolve the 'hit' polymer.
Cut parts of the catheter into cylindrical pieces 5 mm in length.
Measure the cylindrical pieces with a digital Vernier calliper.

Immerse catheter pieces in acetic acid, ammonia, acetone, acetonitrile, diethyl ether, tetrahydrofuran (THF), dimethylformamide (DMF), N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), ethanol, methanol, ethylene glycol, toluene, and xylene.
Evaluate the solvents for 12 hours visually for integrity of catheter and clarity of solvent.
Choose a solvent that does not cause the catheters to swell or disintegrate or result in a turbid solvent.
The chosen solvent must dissolve the 'hit' polymers.
Prepare 2.5% (w/v) polymer solutions in acetone, or other suitable solvent as determined in section 8.
Place 5 mm catheter pieces into small glass vials (5 ml).
Immerse catheter pieces in 1 ml of the polymer solution for 2 min.
Remove excess polymer solution from catheter pieces.
Dry the catheter pieces overnight in a vacuum oven at 40 °C.
Prepare inoculum by mixing thawed bacterial stocks to give approximately 10^6 cells of each species in 50 ml LB6.
Sterilize coated and uncoated catheter pieces with UV light for 30 min.
Incubate the sterilized catheters with 1 ml inoculated LB in a 24-well plate at 37 °C for 3 days with gentle agitation.
Wash the catheters with PBS twice, using 2 ml per wash.
Fix the bacteria on the catheter pieces with 10% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 30 min.
Wash the fixed samples with PBS using 1 ml.
Stain the bacteria on the catheter pieces with DAPI (1 µg ml−1) for 20 min.
Wash the stained samples with PBS using 1 ml.

Obtain confocal images of the catheter pieces using a blue diode laser at 405 nm, detector range 414 to 502 nm, pinhole set to Airy1, image size 1,024 × 1,024 pixels, voxel width 105.2 nm, and Z-stacks spacing 0.5 µm.
Capture confocal images by stacking 50 images across a 100 µm length of the catheter piece.
Flatten the Z-stacked images in the Z plane using an analysis software to extend depth of field and create a single image of a catheter piece.
Analyze the single image to obtain the area of the catheter covered by bacteria, after background-correction using the 'flatten background' function.
Press a pipette tip into the mid portion of the cut catheter piece to hold it.
Dip the held catheter piece in the polymer solution for approximately 30 seconds.
Dry the coated catheter piece in ambient conditions for 30 minutes.
Apply a second coating by immersing the dried piece back into the polymer solution.
Dry the doubly-coated catheter pieces overnight in ambient conditions.
Wash the UV-treated and bacteria-incubated pieces (n = 3) with PBS twice, using 1 ml per wash.
Transfer washed pieces to 48-well plates containing 10% formaldehyde in PBS for 30 minutes.
Wash the fixed pieces with PBS once more, using 1 ml.
Dry the fixed and washed pieces overnight at room temperature.
Mount dried pieces on stubs with conductive carbon disks.
Gold coat the mounted pieces using a sputter coater.
Obtain images of coated pieces using a scanning electron microscope.
